standard_prerequisites.name: For an inverse system with surjective transition maps having locally nilpotent kernels, an element mapping to a unit in the first ring of the system is a unit, so the kernel of the map to that ring lies in the Jacobson radical
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the residue field map of the limit ring factors through the first ring of the system.

standard_prerequisites.name: A perfect object has finite tor dimension, so its fibres have bounded support
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the interval outside which the fibre cohomology of the limit vanishes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Perfectness of a pseudo-coherent complex is checked on the fibres at the residue fields by the vanishing of their cohomology outside an interval
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the derived limit is perfect from the vanishing just established.

core_obligations: Recall from the pseudo-coherence companion statement that the derived limit is pseudo-coherent and that reduction along the system recovers each object (proof lines 28421-28424).

Consider a surjection from the limit ring onto a residue field with kernel a maximal ideal, and show that every element mapping to a unit in the first ring of the system is a unit in the limit ring, using the locally nilpotent kernel statement, whence the kernel lies in the Jacobson radical by the radical statement (proof lines 28424-28430).

Conclude that the residue field map factors through the first ring of the system, and hence that the fibre of the limit at the residue field is the fibre of the first object, which is perfect by hypothesis and therefore has finite tor dimension (proof lines 28430-28439).

Deduce that the cohomology of the fibre vanishes outside a bounded interval and apply the criterion checking perfectness on the fibres to conclude that the derived limit is perfect, which with the earlier recovery statement gives both assertions (proof lines 28439-28443).
proof_roadmap: Import pseudo-coherence and recovery along the system from the companion statement (proof lines 28421-28424).
Factor the residue field map through the first ring using the unit and radical statements (proof lines 28424-28430).
Identify the fibre of the limit with the fibre of the first object and conclude perfectness by the bounded fibre criterion (proof lines 28430-28443).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the perfect analogue of the pseudo-coherence statement for derived limits over inverse systems of rings with surjective transition maps having locally nilpotent kernels, and it asserts both perfectness of the limit and recovery of each object by reduction (statement lines 28400-28419). The proof imports pseudo-coherence and recovery from the companion statement, and its own content is the reduction of perfectness to a single fibre computation: any element mapping to a unit in the first ring of the system is a unit in the limit, so the residue field map factors through that ring and the fibre of the limit is the fibre of the first object, which is perfect and hence of finite tor dimension, after which the bounded fibre criterion gives perfectness (proof lines 28421-28443). The factorization of the residue field map through the first ring is the step that makes one fibre computation suffice. The counted statement carries the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble defines as comment-type, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed; the five references are carried as navigation stubs.
